public_rationale: July evaluations identify a substantial gap on unfamiliar reasoning tasks that humans can solve. The July 24 benchmark leader still scored 30.2% on ARC-AGI-3. These results support the claim that publicly evaluated AI had not achieved reliable superiority across intellectual activities. High scores on other benchmarks do not remove the demonstrated gap.
limitations: ARC-AGI-3 measures a particular kind of adaptive reasoning, not intelligence as a whole.
The July 24 ARC-AGI-3 evaluation used High reasoning effort because the testing window was short.
The evidence concerns publicly evaluated systems and does not verify the separate Marcus–Brundage task count.

our_interpretation: Assess the factual assertion that current AI had not surpassed expert humans across intellectual activities. Laughable is rhetorical emphasis, not a separate measurable claim.
The contextual definition supplies the capability standard, not a conditional forecast.
The plain reading requires reliable breadth of capability. Strong performance in selected domains alone is insufficient.
Use July 1–28, 2026, for current capabilities. There is no regular reporting period for frontier capability.
The claim does not require independently grading the separate assertion about how many Marcus–Brundage tasks AI could perform.
criteria.support_condition: Credible July evaluations show that leading AI systems still have substantial deficits on intellectual tasks humans can perform.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, independently validated evaluations establish an AI system that reliably matches or surpasses expert humans across intellectual activities, including unfamiliar tasks.
